title: Legal Lead
description:
FlytBase

Build and own FlytBase’s global legal function - lead enterprise deals, expansion, IP, and fundraising readiness from our Pune HQ.

Operations

Pune, India

Full-time

5 - 8 years

### **What We Do**

FlytBase is the global category leader in Physical AI for Large sites. FlytBase’s drone autonomy platform powers mission-critical operations across 400+ enterprise sites in 70+ countries. Our customers include Fortune 500 leaders such as Shell, CSX, UK Police, Airbus, Anglo American, Dole, and Statnett. FlytBase has its presence in 70+ countries with offices in the US and Pune, India. FlytBase is building the nervous system for large industrial sites. We operate at AI speed - autonomy and intelligence at our core. Our lean team thrives in a high-agency, high-velocity environment where AI is not a side project; it is the operating system for how we think, build, and grow.

### **The Role**

You’ll be FlytBase’s first in-house Legal Lead, building the legal function from scratch while working directly with the founders. Your job is to make it easier, safer, and faster for the company to grow globally, across enterprise contracting, international expansion, IP, and future fundraising. On any given day, you might be negotiating a complex liability/indemnity package with a Fortune 500 customer in the US, untangling IP and data rights in a new product integration, structuring an employer-of-record setup for a new country, or making sure our cap table and approvals are diligence-ready. You’ll know when to pull in external specialists, and you’ll own the questions, decisions, and follow-through. If you enjoy building clean, scalable legal systems for fast-moving tech businesses, and you want your work to directly influence deals, product decisions, and how we enter new markets, this role will keep you on your toes.

### **What You'll Own**

• International enterprise contracting: Lead end-to-end negotiations with large enterprise customers, their in-house counsel, procurement, and external attorneys, especially in the US and Europe. • Drafting & negotiation: Own master agreements, SaaS/subscription terms, partner and reseller agreements, DPAs, security addenda, and vendor contracts—often starting from customer paper. • Risk & remedies: Resolve hard issues on liability caps, IP indemnities, warranties, SLAs, data rights, termination, governing law, and dispute resolution with a commercial, not academic, lens. • Deal structuring: Work with sales, engineering, security, and finance to align commitments with what we can actually deliver, and build pragmatic fallback positions that help close good business. • Fundraising readiness: Keep corporate records, equity documentation, approvals, and IP ownership evidence clean and diligence-ready for future financing rounds. • Corporate transactions: Partner with founders, finance, and external counsel on term sheets, investment documents, diligence responses, closing mechanics, and ongoing corporate governance. • Global people & entities: Help structure international hiring (employees, contractors, EOR) and support new entities, intercompany arrangements, and local compliance with specialist input. • IP & disputes: Protect FlytBase’s software and inventions in all our contracts, separate platform IP from customer deliverables and data, and coordinate specialist counsel on patents, trademarks, licensing demands, and infringement disputes. • Legal systems & templates: Build templates, playbooks, approval rules, contract records, and dashboards that give the business clear visibility into obligations and reduce turnaround times. • AI-native legal ops: Experiment with AI and automation to draft, redline, summarise, and track contracts—while enforcing disciplined confidentiality, verification, and human review.

### **Best Suited For**

• Seasoned tech counsel with 5–8 years (or equivalent) post-qualification experience in enterprise technology/SaaS contracting across multiple jurisdictions. • Hands-on negotiator who has personally led complex deals with US and/or European customer counsel—beyond NDAs and boilerplate vendor agreements. • Commercial problem-solver who can explain trade-offs in plain English and recommend which risks to accept, push back on, or escalate (and why). • Corporate generalist with experience supporting fundraising, keeping cap tables and approvals clean, and working through investment documents with external counsel. • IP-aware lawyer comfortable with software, cloud, data, open-source, and AI-related IP questions, even if you’re not a patent litigator. • Operator who can run independently, manage competing priorities, and work directly with founders, sales, engineering, security, and people ops. • AI-fluent professional who actively uses AI tools to draft, research, and build systems—without outsourcing your judgment or ethics to them. • Builder who has either created or significantly improved legal processes, templates, and playbooks in a fast-moving company.

### **What Makes You a Flyter**

• Radical ownership: You don’t just spot legal issues—you drive them from identification to resolution, including the messy operational bits. • Business-first thinking: You see contracts and structures as tools to enable smart risk-taking and growth, not to block anything that moves. • Clarity under pressure: You can take a dense redline or complex cross-border issue and explain it in two clear options with a recommendation. • High candor, low ego: You give direct advice to senior leaders, invite pushback, and change your mind fast when new facts show up. • Systems over heroics: You’d rather fix the process and template once than fight the same negotiation fire ten times. • Curiosity for new terrain: When you hit a novel jurisdiction or AI/IP problem, you dig in, get specialist help where needed, and level up fast.

### **What We Don't Want**

• Deal spectators who “review and comment” from the sidelines but avoid taking the lead on live negotiations with customer counsel. • Policy purists who default to saying no, cite theoretical risk, and don’t offer commercially workable alternatives or phased approaches. • Title-chasers who want to “head legal” in name but aren’t willing to do the hands-on drafting, redlining, and process-building work. • Solo geniuses who resist using templates, playbooks, AI tools, or checklists and prefer everything to live in their inbox and memory. • Jurisdictional overconfidence who wing cross-border employment, tax, or IP issues without knowing when to bring in specialist advice. • Slow movers who need weeks to turn around standard agreements or who treat every routine negotiation like a zero-sum courtroom battle.

### **Why FlytBase?**

• Build the function: Architect FlytBase’s legal function from day zero - templates, playbooks, tools, and governance, rather than inheriting someone else’s mess. • Front-row seat to scale: Work directly with founders on the deals, structures, and financings that shape how Physical AI scales across 400+ sites in 70+ countries. • High-agency environment: Operate with real decision-making power, not just markup authority, your judgment will directly influence revenue, product, and hiring. • Complex global work: Navigate US/EU enterprise contracts, cross-border hiring, IP, and future fundraising in a single role instead of being siloed. • AI-native legal practice: Experiment with AI and automation in your own workflows at a company where autonomy and intelligence are the core product, not a side project. • In-person energy: Work from our Pune office with high-cadence collaboration, fast feedback loops, and a team that cares about being Happy, Healthy, and High-Performing.

### **The Perks**

• High agency team and sense of purpose • International Travel - we travel to all 6 continents (sorry, no business in Antarctica yet) • Thought leadership & public speaking opportunities at online & physical events • No-cap budget for AI tools, courses, or experiments • Latest tech stack and tools - whatever helps you move faster • Unlimited leave policy & flexible working hours (no punch-in/out) • A damn good team to work with

### **Who You'll Work With**

You’ll work directly with the founders and the operations leadership team, sitting close to sales, finance, people ops, and engineering. You’ll also coordinate with our external legal advisers and specialist counsel across corporate, employment, IP, and international matters.

### **Ready to Fly?**

If you want to build a legal function that actually helps a global AI company move faster, and you’re ready to own the hard calls, apply with specific examples of the toughest deals and decisions you’ve led.

title: Manager of Contract Operations
description:
Perforce is a community of collaborative experts, problem solvers, and possibility seekers who believe work should be both challenging and fun. We are proud to inspire creativity, foster belonging, support collaboration, and encourage wellness. At Perforce, you’ll work with and learn from some of the best and brightest in business. Before you know it, you’ll be in the middle of a rewarding career at a company headed in one direction: upward.

With a global footprint spanning more than 80 countries and including over 75% of the Fortune 100, Perforce Software, Inc. is trusted by the world’s leading brands to deliver solutions for the toughest challenges. The best run DevOps teams in the world choose Perforce.

### **About the Role**

The Legal Team is seeking a Manager of Contract Operations to lead and build the Commercial Transactions team in Pune, India. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and demonstrates strong leadership, problem-solving, independent decision-making, and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

The role involves managing legal request intake and distribution from Sales, balancing contract workloads, handling escalations, and personally drafting, redlining, and negotiating complex commercial agreements with customers, partners, and vendors. The individual will uphold the highest standards of judgment, integrity, and ethical leadership while managing risk, developing a high-performing team, and supporting Perforce’s business objectives.

Working closely with the US-based contracts team and cross-functional stakeholders - including Sales, Sales Operations, Customer Success, Customer Support, Professional Services, Information Security, Finance, and Revenue Operations - the Manager will ensure global contracting alignment, effective contract negotiation, and compliance with contractual obligations. The position reports to the Managing Counsel in the United States

### **What You'll Do:**

* Serve as the first Legal Team hire in Pune and build, hire, onboard, train, mentor, and lead a local commercial contracts team while driving a collaborative and high-performing team culture.
* Manage the legal request queue from Sales through Salesforce, triage and prioritise incoming work, balance workloads, monitor service levels and turnaround times, and act as the primary escalation point for complex legal, commercial, and negotiation matters.
* Draft, review, negotiate, and execute complex commercial agreements, including on-premise software licences, SaaS agreements, professional services agreements, channel and partner agreements, data processing agreements, and other contracts supporting go-to-market activities.
* Partner closely with US-based legal colleagues and cross-functional stakeholders to align negotiation standards, playbooks, approval processes, contract governance, legal operations, AI-enabled workflow improvements, contract repository management, and risk-based commercial decision-making.

### **What You'll Bring:**

* Undergraduate degree required; law degree (LL.B. or equivalent) preferred, with at least 10 years of hands-on experience drafting and negotiating technology, software licensing, cloud-hosted software, SaaS, and platform-as-a-service agreements.
* At least 3 years of people-management experience, including direct leadership of contracts professionals, with demonstrated success building, scaling, recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and developing high-performing teams.
* Experience managing high-volume legal intake processes within Salesforce, a contract lifecycle management platform, or a similar system, together with strong commercial negotiation skills across enterprise software transactions, revenue models, risk assessment, and global contracting practices.
* Excellent drafting, communication, leadership, project-management, and organisational skills; experience working in-house for a global technology company strongly preferred. Experience with Artificial Intelligence tools is required, legal AI tools are a plus, and willingness to support US collaboration hours during onboarding is essential.

*All employees are expected to demonstrate AI fluency appropriate to their role and level, including responsible use of AI tools, sound judgment, and adherence to company AI governance and security policy standards.*

**Come work with us! Our team members are valued for their contributions, introduced to new opportunities, and rewarded well**. Perforce combines the experience and rewards of a start-up with the security of an established and privately held profitable company.

If you are passionate about the technology that impacts our day-to-day lives and want to work with talented and dedicated people across the globe, apply today!

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

As part of our EY – ER - Regulatory Compliance team, you will help the clients by understanding their business needs and delivering solutions in accordance with the EY guidelines & methodologies. As a Regulatory Compliance Senior actively establish, maintain and strengthen internal and external relationships. In line with our commitment to quality, you will consistently drive projects to completion with high quality deliverables, achieve operational efficiency, proactively identify and raise risks with the client as well as EY senior management team and lead internal initiatives.

  

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking an experienced Manager (Validation/Tester – Veeva) to lead validation, testing activities and compliance across various Veeva modules, regulated and business critical computerized systems for global pharmaceutical clients. The ideal candidate will ensure compliance with global regulatory standards (FDA, EMA, MHRA) and drive strategic initiatives for business process transformation and operational excellence.

  

**Your Key Responsibilities**

* Lead CSA/CSV strategy in collaboration with Governance and risk-based validation approach for the Veeva Vault platform, balancing modern CSA principles (critical thinking, risk-based test coverage) with CSV rigor where required for specific vaults/regulatory contexts.
* Perform risk assessments on platform changes (configuration, integration, releases) to determine appropriate validation rigor and evidence requirements per change.
* Define validation/testing evidence requirements in partnership with the QA Engineer role — ensuring test coverage decisions are risk-justified and audit-defensible.
* Review and approve validation deliverables (validation plans, risk assessments, test evidence, validation summary reports) before closure.
* Ensure platform changes comply with applicable regulations (21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, GAMP 5) and internal Computerized System Validation policies.
* Provide compliance guidance to internal Leads and vendor team members on how CSA principles apply to specific configuration/integration scenarios.
* Support internal/external audits and health authority inspections — act as the platform's validation SME during inspection readiness and response.
* Partner with QA/Change Management to ensure Change Control records carry appropriate validation justification and evidence.
* Stay current on evolving CSA guidance (e.g., FDA's CSA draft guidance) and industry practice, advising the CoE on policy updates.

  

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Biotechnology, Engineering, or related field.
* 8+ years in CSV within the pharmaceutical, life sciences or consulting organizations.
* Comfortable working with distributed teams across India, Prague, and US time zones.
Strong influencing skills to drive practice change (CSV* CSA) across a delivery team that includes multiple other vendor roles.

  

**Must-Have Skills & Attributes**

* Experience in Computer System Validation, with demonstrated leadership transitioning teams from traditional CSV to CSA practices.
* Deep knowledge of GAMP 5 (2nd edition), FDA CSA guidance, 21 CFR Part 11, and EU Annex 11.
* Experience defining risk-based testing/validation strategies that reduce documentation/testing burden without compromising compliance.
* Experience validating cloud/SaaS platforms (Veeva Vault experience strongly preferred) in a GxP environment.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections/audits as a validation SME.
* Strong stakeholder influencing skills — this role must drive adoption of CSA thinking across delivery teams (Configuration, Integration, QA) who may default to legacy CSV habits.
* Experience partnering with QA/Test Automation teams to align risk assessments with automated test coverage decisions.
* Strong project management, problem solving and communication skills
* Apply structured and analytical thinking to improve delivery efficiency and client outcomes.

  

**Good-to-Have Skills & Attributes**

* Prior experience specifically validating Veeva Vault implementations (any vault — Clinical, RIM, QMS, Safety, Medical, CRM).
* Experience building or updating an organization's CSA policy/SOP framework.
* Experience with Veeva Vault QMS/QualityDocs as the vehicle for validation documentation.
* ISPE GAMP 5 training/certification
* High attention to detail and analytical thinking.
* Familiarity with emerging regulatory trends, such as CSA or digital validation approaches.
* Adaptability to changing regulatory and business environments.

  

**Preferred Certifications**

* Certified Software Quality Engineer (CSQE), Certified Software Quality Assurance (CSQA)
* Information Security or Risk Management certifications.
* Any Veeva Quality certification.

  

**What we look for**

* A Team of people with commercial acumen, technical experience and enthusiasm to learn new things in this fast-moving environment with consulting skills.
* An opportunity to be a part of market-leading, multi-disciplinary team of 1400 + professionals, in the only integrated global transaction business worldwide.
* Opportunities to work with EY Consulting practices globally with leading businesses across a range of industries.

  

**What working at EY offers**

At EY, we’re dedicated to helping our clients, from startups to Fortune 500 companies — and the work we do with them is as varied as they are.

You get to work with inspiring and meaningful projects. Our focus is education and coaching alongside practical experience to ensure your personal development. We value our employees and you will be able to control your own development with an individual progression plan. You will quickly grow into a responsible role with challenging and stimulating assignments. Moreover, you will be part of an interdisciplinary environment that emphasizes high quality and knowledge exchange. Plus, we offer:

* **Support, coaching and feedback from some of the most engaging colleagues around**

EY exists to build a better working world, helping to create long-term value for clients, people and society and build trust in the capital markets.

Enabled by data and technology, diverse EY teams in over 150 countries provide trust through assurance and help clients grow, transform and operate.

Working across assurance, consulting, law, strategy, tax and transactions, EY teams ask better questions to find new answers for the complex issues facing our world today.

-

Role Purpose

The role is responsible for legal evaluation of bid/tender documents, contract risk assessment, and end-to-end management of arbitration and dispute resolution processes with customers and vendors.

The incumbent will safeguard the organization’s legal and commercial interests while ensuring compliance, risk mitigation, and structured dispute resolution.

-

Key Responsibilities (KRAs)

1️⃣ Bid & Tender Legal Evaluation

* Review and evaluate RFPs, RFQs, tender documents, and bid submissions

* Identify legal, contractual, and commercial risks

* Highlight deviation clauses and recommend mitigation strategies

* Draft and review bid qualifications and legal clarifications

* Support Go/No-Go decisions from a legal risk perspective

* Ensure compliance with statutory, regulatory, and contractual obligations

-

2️⃣ Contract Drafting & Commercial Agreements

* Draft, review, and negotiate:

o Customer contracts

o Vendor agreements

o NDAs, MoUs, SLAs, AMC contracts

o Turnkey / project agreements

* Ensure appropriate risk allocation (indemnity, liability caps, penalties, LD clauses)

* Standardize contract templates and maintain clause repository

* Advise business and commercial teams on contractual exposure

-

3️⃣ Arbitration & Dispute Management

* Manage arbitration matters with customers and vendors

* Coordinate with external counsel and represent company interests

* Prepare legal notices, replies, claims, and counter-claims

* Compile documentation and evidence for arbitration proceedings

* Track dispute exposure, timelines, and potential financial impact

* Advise management on settlement strategies and litigation risk

* Maintain dispute MIS and legal risk registers

-

4️⃣ Legal Risk Advisory

* Provide proactive legal advice to Sales, Projects, Procurement & Commercial teams

* Assess contractual risks in large turnkey and long-term projects

* Recommend structured risk mitigation strategies

* Support internal investigations and compliance reviews where required

-

5️⃣ Governance & Compliance

* Ensure compliance with applicable laws including:

o Companies Act

o Contract Act

o Arbitration & Conciliation Act

o Industry-specific regulations

* Maintain centralized contract documentation

* Support internal and external audits

-

Key Risk Indicators (KRIs)

* Acceptance of high-risk contractual clauses without mitigation

* Escalation of disputes due to contractual gaps

* Financial exposure from arbitration awards

* Liquidated damages triggered due to contractual weaknesses

* Delays in legal response to notices or claims

* Inadequate documentation impacting dispute outcomes

-

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

* Turnaround time (TAT) for contract reviews

* Reduction in contractual risk exposure

* Favorable arbitration outcomes / settlements

* Reduction in dispute escalation cases

* Standardization and implementation of contract templates

-

Education & Qualification Parameters

Mandatory:

* LLB (Bachelor of Laws)

Preferred:

* LLM (Corporate / Commercial Law preferred)

* 5–10 years of experience in commercial contracts and arbitration

* Experience in telecom / infrastructure / project-driven industry

* Strong understanding of Arbitration & Conciliation Act and commercial dispute handling

-

Key Competencies

Functional:

* Contract drafting & negotiation

* Legal risk assessment

* Arbitration handling & dispute management

* Commercial awareness

* Regulatory knowledge

Behavioral:

* Strong analytical and risk-oriented mindset

* Negotiation and influencing ability

* High attention to detail

* Ability to work under pressure

* Strong stakeholder management

-

Interface Departments

* Sales & Business Development

* Projects & Operations

* Procurement & Commercial

* Finance

* External Legal Counsel

* Customers & Vendors

title: Compliance Engineer
description:
**Compliance Engineer**, Fonazo

**The role:**

Fonazo is hiring a Compliance Engineer to own the Global Compliance Engine: the controls that let an AI voice agent place a lawful call in any country it operates in.

Fonazo is an AI Voice Agent Builder. A business launches a multilingual voice agent in about two minutes, and every call that agent makes passes through compliance controls enforced in the product, not in a policy document. The engine is live in five countries today.

**Country - Regimes enforced in product**

India - TRAI, DoT, DLT, DPDP Act 2023

United States - FCC, TCPA, FTC

United Kingdom - Ofcom, ICO, PECR

Germany - BNetzA, UWG

France - ARCEP, DGCCRF

The next markets are the UAE, Spain, and Italy. This role turns each new country from a legal reading into shipped, tested, auditable controls, and makes compliance the reason enterprises choose Fonazo.

Reports to - Founder and CEO

Base - Pune, India

Type - Full time

Experience - 4+ years in compliance engineering, GRC engineering, or regulated product engineering

**What the role owns**

* The Global Compliance Engine rule set for every live country: consent capture, calling windows, do-not-call and preference register scrubbing, caller identification, AI disclosure, sender and template registration, call frequency limits, and recording consent.
* Country launches. Each new market moves from regulatory text to product requirements, shipped controls, automated tests, and a customer-facing control summary.
* Compliance as code. Rules are versioned, tested, and deployed like software, so a regulatory change becomes a release, not a memo.
* Data protection engineering under DPDP, GDPR, and UK GDPR: data mapping, retention and deletion, data subject requests, cross-border transfer controls, and processor obligations.
* Audit programmes. Readiness, evidence automation, and auditor management for independent attestations such as SOC 2 and ISO 27001, carried through to formal closure.
* Audit trails. Every call carries a tamper-evident record of which controls applied and why.
* Enterprise deal support: security and compliance questionnaires, data processing agreements, and regulator-facing documentation, answered in days.
* Regulatory watch across all live and planned markets, with impact assessed and scheduled before the effective date.
* Telecom registration workflows with operators and aggregators in each country.

**How Fonazo positions compliance**

Fonazo states precisely which controls the product enforces and proves each one with evidence. The person in this role protects that standard in every external document, sales conversation, and contract.

**What the candidate brings**

* 4+ years building compliance controls into a software product, or running GRC engineering for a regulated technology company.
* Working knowledge of telemarketing and electronic communications regulation in at least two of India, the US, the UK, and the EU.
* Hands-on data protection experience under GDPR or DPDP, including records of processing, impact assessments, and deletion pipelines.
* Direct experience taking a company through an independent security or privacy audit from readiness to report.
* The ability to read primary regulation and write an unambiguous product requirement and test case from it.
* Engineering skill to script, query, and automate: policy as code, evidence collection, control monitoring.
* Clear writing for three audiences: engineers, enterprise legal teams, and regulators.
* Experience with AI governance frameworks such as the EU AI Act, NISTAI RMF, or ISO 42001 is a strong advantage.
* A background in telecom, fintech, healthtech, or contact centre technology is an advantage.

**Stack and tooling**

Fonazo does not publish its internal architecture. Fit is assessed on what the candidate has run in production, so every application should state:

* Cloud environments and deployment models operated in, and at what scale.
* GRC, evidence automation, and control monitoring tools used, and which were built in house.
* Policy as code and rules engine approaches used, with one example of a regulation turned into an automated control.
* Languages and data tooling used for compliance automation.
* Consent management, preference register, and data subject request systems built or integrated.
* Telephony, messaging, or communications systems worked with.
* Frameworks audited against, the candidate's exact role in each audit, and the outcome.
* The stack the candidate would choose to build a multi-country compliance engine from zero, and why.

**What success looks like**

Timeframe - Outcome

30 days - Full control inventory for all five live countries, mapped to source regulation, with gaps ranked

90 days - Automated test coverage for every live control and a standard enterprise compliance pack used by sales

180 days - One new country launched end to end and one independent audit programme in active fieldwork

12 months - New country launch reduced to a repeatable playbook measured in weeks

**Why this role**

Compliance here is the product, shipped in code and sold as a reason to buy.

Ownership of a multi-country engine at a stage where every design decision is still open.

Work that sits at the front of AI voice regulation in eight markets.

Direct line to the founder and a seat in enterprise deals.

Pay: ₹30,000.00 - ₹80,000.00 per month
